name: Electric Bicycle
description: A bicycle or tricycle with fully operable pedals, a seat or saddle, and an electric motor of less than 750 watts, in one of three classes: Class 1 and Class 3 pedal-assist up to 20 and 28 mph, and Class 2 throttle-assisted up to 20 mph.

restrictions.rule: A bicycle or tricycle with fully operable pedals, a seat or saddle, and a motor of less than 750 watts
Class 1 assists only while the rider pedals and stops at 20 mph; Class 2's motor can propel it without pedaling, up to 20 mph; Class 3 assists only while pedaling and stops at 28 mph
The motor must disengage or stop when the rider stops pedaling or applies the brakes
Carries a permanent label stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage
Must not be modified to change its motor-powered speed or engagement unless the label is replaced to match
Meets the CPSC's bicycle requirements (16 CFR part 1512)

restrictions.citation: Florida Statutes §316.20655, as amended by chapter 2025-149

restrictions.rule: A local government may set minimum ages by ordinance and require riders to carry government-issued photo ID
restrictions.citation: Florida Statutes §316.20655, as amended by chapter 2025-149

restrictions.rule: Riders and passengers under 16 must wear a bicycle helmet
Carries no more people than it is designed or equipped for, except that an adult may carry a child secured in a backpack or sling
Has the rights and duties of a bicycle and may be ridden wherever bicycles may, including streets, highways, bike lanes and multi-use paths
On a sidewalk the rider must yield to pedestrians and give an audible signal before passing
A local government may regulate it on streets, highways and sidewalks, and restrict or ban it on paths, trails, beaches and dunes
restrictions.citation: Florida Statutes §316.20655, as amended by chapter 2025-149

restrictions.rule: Not a motor vehicle or a moped: no driver's license, registration, title or insurance, and exempt from off-highway vehicle rules

One with a motor of 750 watts or more, or outside the three classes, isn't an electric bicycle: it is a motorized scooter if it can't exceed 20 mph; a moped, which needs a driver's license and registration, if it has pedals and a motor of 2 brake horsepower (1,500 W) or less that can't pass 30 mph; and otherwise a motorcycle, which needs a motorcycle endorsement, title and registration
